# DUST-20 documentation

> DUST-20 binds every token unit to an exact number of satoshis. Deploy and mint are inscriptions; every later movement is an ordinary Bitcoin spend of the satoshis that carry the units.

- Site: https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/
- Source: https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/dust-20
- Machine-readable protocol model: https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/docs.json
- Conformance fixtures: https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/conformance.json
- Chain: Bitcoin
- Classification: Satoshi-denominated colored UTXO fungibility protocol
- Last updated: 2026-08-18

## How to read this document

Every statement carries a provenance label. Nothing below is asserted as a protocol rule merely to make the documentation look complete.

- VERIFIED: Documented in the legacy DUST-20 specification and enforced by the Bitcoin Universe production indexer. Both sources agree.
- UNIVERSE: Enforced by the Bitcoin Universe production indexer. The legacy specification does not settle this point, so an independent implementation may differ.
- LEGACY: Stated by legacy DUST-20 documentation. Superseded, narrowed, or not enforced identically by the current implementation.
- IMPL: The behaviour of one application or service. Useful evidence, but not a protocol rule. Do not rely on it across implementations.
- UNRESOLVED: No authoritative answer exists. Documented as an open question rather than invented. Stop before an irreversible step.

## Sources

- Legacy DUST-20 specification — https://dust-20.gitbook.io/dust20/readme.md
  Documents the deploy and mint payloads and a colored-UTXO transfer example.
- Bitcoin Universe production indexer — https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio
  index-dust20 — reconstructs colored UTXO ownership from Bitcoin Core and a shared Ord 0.29 instance.
- Bitcoin Universe Inscribe — https://inscribe.bitcoinuniverse.io
  Application that builds DUST-20 deploy and mint inscriptions.
- This documentation repository — https://github.com/bitcoinuniverseio/dust-20
  Source of the published documentation and its conformance fixtures.

- [Playground](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/playground.html): Build and validate DUST-20 deploy and mint payloads in your browser with exact integer arithmetic. No wallet, no keys, no signing.
- [Transactions](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/transactions.html): Visualize how DUST-20 units follow satoshis through a Bitcoin spend: partial sends, colored change, merges, fee separation and the constructions that burn units.

## Operations

### Deploy [VERIFIED]

Creates a ticker and fixes the satoshi backing rule for every one of its units.

A deploy declares the maximum supply, the exact satoshis that back one unit, the total backing that follows from those two numbers, and an optional per-mint satoshi cap.

Required fields: p, op, tick, supply, unit_sats, max_sats
Optional fields: lim_sats

### Mint [VERIFIED]

Creates units in a Bitcoin output whose value equals the declared satoshi backing.

A mint resolves an accepted deployment, states an amount of whole units, and states the satoshis backing them. The Bitcoin output that carries the inscription must hold exactly that many satoshis.

Required fields: p, op, tick, amt, sats
Optional fields: none

### Transfer [UNIVERSE]

An ordinary Bitcoin spend. There is no transfer inscription.

Units follow the satoshis that carry them, in ordinal first-in-first-out order. A whole unit that lands entirely inside one supported output survives; anything else is burned. No JSON payload participates.

### Burn [UNIVERSE]

A derived outcome, not an operation anyone writes.

Units are burned when the satoshis carrying them are paid to miners as fees, sent to an output the indexer cannot attribute to an address, or split so that no whole unit fits inside a single output.

## Field reference

### p [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy, mint
- Type: string
- Required
- Constraint: Exactly "dust-20".
- Example: dust-20
- Rule: Content whose "p" is not the literal dust-20 is not a DUST-20 message and is ignored.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: The protocol identifier is matched literally. There is no aliasing, casing tolerance, or versioned variant.

### op [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy, mint
- Type: string
- Required
- Constraint: Exactly "deploy" or "mint".
- Example: deploy
- Rule: Any other operation value is rejected. No transfer or burn inscription exists.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: The production indexer rejects an inscription whose op is anything other than deploy or mint, including op: "transfer".

### tick [UNIVERSE]

- Operations: deploy, mint
- Type: string
- Required
- Constraint: Unicode NFC text, 1 to 64 UTF-8 bytes, with no control characters, whitespace, or the URL delimiters / ? # \.
- Example: dust
- Rule: The identity of a ticker is its NFC form case-folded to lower case. A mint resolves against that folded identity.
- Provenance: Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: The legacy guide says the ticker is not limited to four bytes but does not settle case handling or duplicates. The production indexer settles both: identity is NFC plus lower-case folding, and the first valid deployment of an identity wins. Later deploys of the same identity are rejected.

### supply [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy
- Type: integer string
- Required
- Constraint: Canonical positive integer string matching /^[1-9][0-9]*$/, at most 2^128 - 1.
- Example: 1000000
- Rule: Total whole units that may ever be minted for this ticker.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: No leading zeros, no sign, no decimal point, no exponent, no whitespace. DUST-20 balances have zero decimal places, so a unit is always a whole number.

### unit_sats [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy
- Type: integer string
- Required
- Constraint: Canonical positive integer string, at most Bitcoin’s monetary supply of 2,100,000,000,000,000 satoshis.
- Example: 546
- Rule: The exact number of satoshis that back one unit for the entire life of the ticker.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: 546 is a common documented example because it is Bitcoin’s usual dust threshold for P2WPKH. It is not a default. A payload that omits unit_sats is rejected — never assume 546.

### max_sats [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy
- Type: integer string
- Required
- Constraint: Canonical positive integer string that equals supply × unit_sats and does not exceed 2,100,000,000,000,000.
- Example: 546000000
- Rule: Rejected unless it equals supply × unit_sats exactly, computed with exact integer arithmetic.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: This is a redundancy check, not an independent quantity. It exists so a reader can detect a builder that computed the backing with floating point or the wrong unit size. See the reconciliation note about earlier reports that this field was optional.

### lim_sats [VERIFIED]

- Operations: deploy
- Type: integer string
- Optional
- Constraint: Optional canonical non-negative integer string, at most max_sats. Omitted or "0" means no per-mint limit.
- Example: 54600
- Rule: When present and greater than zero, every mint of this ticker must satisfy sats ≤ lim_sats.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: The cap is expressed in satoshis, not units. The equivalent unit cap is lim_sats ÷ unit_sats. A lim_sats that is not a whole multiple of unit_sats simply makes the effective unit cap the floor of that division.

### amt [VERIFIED]

- Operations: mint
- Type: integer string
- Required
- Constraint: Canonical positive integer string matching /^[1-9][0-9]*$/, at most 2^128 - 1.
- Example: 100
- Rule: Whole units to create. Rejected if previously minted units plus amt would exceed supply.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: Zero, negative, fractional, and leading-zero values are rejected outright.

### sats [VERIFIED]

- Operations: mint
- Type: integer string
- Required
- Constraint: Canonical positive integer string that equals amt × unit_sats of the resolved deployment.
- Example: 54600
- Rule: Rejected unless it equals amt × unit_sats, and unless the Bitcoin output carrying the inscription holds exactly this many satoshis.
- Provenance: Legacy DUST-20 specification + Bitcoin Universe production indexer
- Notes: Three numbers must agree: the deployment ratio, the sats field in the JSON, and the real output value on Bitcoin. A one-satoshi difference invalidates the mint.

## Formulas

- max_sats = supply × unit_sats [VERIFIED]
  Total backing is supply multiplied by the satoshis behind one unit. Example: 1,000,000 units × 546 sats = 546,000,000 sats
- sats = amt × unit_sats [VERIFIED]
  The satoshis a mint declares are the units it creates multiplied by the unit size. Example: 100 units × 546 sats = 54,600 sats
- output_value = sats [VERIFIED]
  The Bitcoin output that carries the mint inscription must hold exactly the declared satoshis. Example: A mint declaring 54,600 sats must sit in an output worth exactly 54,600 sats.
- mint_unit_cap = ⌊ lim_sats ÷ unit_sats ⌋ [UNIVERSE]
  A satoshi cap per mint implies a whole-unit cap per mint. Example: 54,600 ÷ 546 = 100 units per mint
- input_units = surviving_units + burned_units [UNIVERSE]
  Units leaving an input either land whole inside a supported output or are burned. Nothing else can happen to them. Example: 91 units in → 10 to the receiver + 81 as change + 0 burned
- output_backing = units_in_output × unit_sats [UNIVERSE]
  Every output carrying units must hold at least the satoshis those whole units occupy, positioned so each unit fits entirely inside it. Example: 81 units × 546 = 44,226 sats of backing
- fee = Σ inputs − Σ outputs [UNIVERSE]
  The miner fee is whatever the transaction does not pay out. Any colored satoshi that falls into that gap is burned, so fees must be funded by ordinary bitcoin. Example: Fund the fee from a separate cardinal input, never by shrinking a colored output.

## Rules

### A payload is a flat JSON object of strings [UNIVERSE]

Inscription content must be valid UTF-8 and a single flat JSON object whose every value is a string. Nested objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and null are rejected. So are duplicate keys, trailing content after the closing brace, and content larger than 4096 bytes.

### Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored [UNIVERSE]

Each operation declares an exact key set. A deploy carrying an extra field, or a mint missing one, does not degrade to a warning — the whole payload is rejected. This is stricter than "ignore what you do not understand" and prevents a malformed message from being read two different ways.

### Integers are canonical decimal strings [VERIFIED]

Every numeric field is a string. Leading zeros, a leading plus, a minus sign, whitespace, decimal points and exponent notation are all rejected. Implementations must use exact integer arithmetic — a 64-bit float silently loses precision above 2^53, well inside the satoshi range.

### The first valid deployment of a ticker wins [UNIVERSE]

Ticker identity is the NFC form of tick, case-folded to lower case. Once a valid deployment exists for an identity, every later deployment of that identity is rejected. "DUST", "dust" and "Dust" are the same ticker.

### A mint resolves exactly one accepted deployment [VERIFIED]

A mint naming a ticker that has no accepted deployment is rejected. The unit size used to check the mint always comes from the resolved deployment, never from the mint payload.

### Mints stop at the declared supply [VERIFIED]

Previously minted units plus amt must not exceed supply. There is no partial fill: a mint that would cross the supply ceiling is rejected in full rather than trimmed.

### The inscription must begin at offset zero of its output [UNIVERSE]

The mint inscription must sit at satoshi offset 0 of the output that carries it, that output must hold exactly sats satoshis, and the output must not already carry a DUST-20 allocation. A mint whose padding does not match its sats field exactly is rejected.

### No transfer inscription is valid [UNIVERSE]

DUST-20 uses inscriptions only for deploy and mint. Movement happens by spending the satoshis that carry the units. An inscription with op: "transfer" is rejected — it does not move anything, and treating it as a transfer is a compatibility error.

### Units follow satoshis in first-in-first-out order [UNIVERSE]

Lay every input value end to end to form one satoshi range, and every output value end to end to form another. A colored allocation occupies a contiguous span in the input range. Each unit is a block of unit_sats satoshis inside that span, and it survives only where a whole block lands inside a single output.

### Three ways units are destroyed [UNIVERSE]

A unit is burned when its satoshis fall past the last output and become the miner fee, when they land in an output the indexer cannot attribute to a supported address, or when they straddle an output boundary so no whole unit fits. Burns are silent on Bitcoin: the transaction confirms normally.

### A partial send needs an explicit colored change output [VERIFIED]

If you spend an allocation of 91 units and send 10, the other 81 need their own output with at least 81 × unit_sats satoshis, aligned so each unit fits whole. Omitting that output does not keep the units — it burns them.

### Fund miner fees with ordinary bitcoin [VERIFIED]

Colored satoshis and fee funding are different concepts. Add a separate cardinal input to pay the fee. Shaving satoshis off a colored output to cover a fee moves the colored range and can burn the units it was meant to carry.

### Merging works when the ticker and unit size match [UNIVERSE]

Several colored inputs of the same ticker can be combined into one output, provided each contributing unit lands whole inside it. Allocations of different tickers keep separate identities even inside one output; they are tracked by their own offsets.

### Reorganizations roll the ledger back [UNIVERSE]

On a reorg the indexer emits invalidations newest first, reverses ledger mutations, restores allocations that had been marked spent, removes allocations the orphaned branch created, and replays the replacement branch. A balance is only as final as the depth it was confirmed at.

### Mempool coverage is partial [UNIVERSE]

The production indexer reports coverage as partial: confirmed history and complete holder snapshots are indexed, but there is no exhaustive mempool feed with a stable pending lifecycle. Unconfirmed DUST-20 state is therefore not a reliable input to an irreversible decision.

## Examples

### Deploy a ticker

```json
{
  "p": "dust-20",
  "op": "deploy",
  "tick": "dust",
  "supply": "1000000",
  "unit_sats": "546",
  "max_sats": "546000000",
  "lim_sats": "54600"
}
```

max_sats is 1,000,000 × 546. lim_sats of 54,600 allows 100 units per mint.

### Deploy without a per-mint cap

```json
{
  "p": "dust-20",
  "op": "deploy",
  "tick": "grain",
  "supply": "21000",
  "unit_sats": "1000",
  "max_sats": "21000000"
}
```

Omitted and "0" both mean no per-mint limit. Use a cap if you want distribution over time.

### Mint at the cap

```json
{
  "p": "dust-20",
  "op": "mint",
  "tick": "dust",
  "amt": "100",
  "sats": "54600"
}
```

The inscription must sit at offset 0 of an output holding exactly 54,600 satoshis.

### Mint a single unit

```json
{
  "p": "dust-20",
  "op": "mint",
  "tick": "dust",
  "amt": "1",
  "sats": "546"
}
```

The smallest valid mint for this deployment is one whole unit.

## Where legacy documentation and the current implementation disagree

### Is max_sats required in a deploy? [VERIFIED]

- Legacy: The legacy profile includes max_sats and frames it as supply × unit_sats. Earlier versions of this documentation additionally reported that the Inscribe builder emitted deploys without max_sats, and labelled the question an unreconciled compatibility split.
- Current: The production indexer requires max_sats. Its deploy key set is exactly p, op, tick, supply, unit_sats, max_sats, with lim_sats optional, and a deploy missing max_sats is rejected rather than inferred.
- Resolution: Resolved in favour of required. Emit max_sats and verify it equals supply × unit_sats. A deploy without it is not indexed by the current implementation.

### Is there a canonical transfer payload? [UNIVERSE]

- Legacy: The legacy guide documents deploy and mint JSON and a colored-UTXO transfer example, but publishes no transfer schema. Earlier documentation listed a transfer inscription as an open question and noted an application emitting a transfer preview containing amt.
- Current: The production indexer accepts no transfer inscription at all. Movement is derived purely from ordinal satoshi flow through ordinary Bitcoin spends.
- Resolution: Resolved: there is no transfer payload. Treat any op: "transfer" inscription as invalid, and treat an application preview containing amt as a user-interface artifact, not a protocol message.

### How are duplicate and differently-cased tickers handled? [UNIVERSE]

- Legacy: The legacy guide states the ticker is not limited to four bytes but does not settle case normalization or which deployment wins when a name is reused.
- Current: Identity is the NFC form case-folded to lower case, bounded to 64 UTF-8 bytes, excluding control characters, whitespace and the delimiters / ? # \. The first valid deployment of an identity wins; later ones are rejected.
- Resolution: Resolved by the current implementation. Independent implementations that compare tickers byte-for-byte will disagree with it, so preserve the original spelling for display and compare on the folded identity.

### What counts as a burn? [UNIVERSE]

- Legacy: The legacy material defines no burn rule, and earlier documentation advised showing recovery actions as potentially allocation-destroying rather than canonical burns.
- Current: Burning is defined precisely and is a consequence of transaction shape, not an instruction: satoshis paid as fees, sent to an unsupported output, or split so no whole unit fits are burned, and the supply accounting records it.
- Resolution: Resolved as a derived outcome. There is still no way to express "burn this" as a message — you burn by constructing a transaction that drops the satoshis.

### Does output order matter? [UNIVERSE]

- Legacy: Earlier documentation listed output ordering as an open question.
- Current: Order matters completely. Allocation is positional: inputs and outputs are concatenated into satoshi ranges in index order, so moving an output changes which units land where.
- Resolution: Resolved: build outputs deliberately and test the exact ordering your builder produces. Reordering outputs is never cosmetic.

### Is there a canonical DUST-20 indexer API? [UNRESOLVED]

- Legacy: No API schema, pagination model, or response versioning is published in the legacy guide.
- Current: The production indexer exposes its own normalized and legacy routes with bearer authentication, stable cursors and explicit coverage labels, but these are one service’s contract.
- Resolution: Unresolved as a standard. Validate remote responses against a schema you control and treat coverage, source identity and observation height as part of every answer.

## Open questions

### Do independent implementations agree with these rules? [UNRESOLVED]

- Why it matters: Most of the transfer, burn and ticker-identity behaviour on this site is settled by one production implementation rather than by a multi-party specification.
- Safe posture: Treat rules marked Current Universe implementation as a working profile. Before relying on them across tools, test against the specific indexer your users will see.

### How many confirmations make a DUST-20 balance safe to act on? [UNRESOLVED]

- Why it matters: The protocol defines no threshold, and reorg handling restores or removes allocations depending on depth.
- Safe posture: Publish your own finality depth, show confirmation counts to users, and never present unconfirmed DUST-20 state as settled.

### What is the pending lifecycle for an unconfirmed DUST-20 movement? [UNRESOLVED]

- Why it matters: The production indexer reports partial coverage precisely because it has no exhaustive mempool feed with stable pending and disappearance handling.
- Safe posture: Do not build balance guarantees on mempool state. Show pending movements as unverified and re-check at confirmation.

### What happens to DUST-20 state when a transaction is replaced? [UNRESOLVED]

- Why it matters: Replace-by-fee can change the output layout, which changes where colored satoshis land — a replacement can burn units the original preserved.
- Safe posture: Re-derive allocation from the transaction that actually confirmed. Never carry forward the pre-replacement interpretation, and never blindly rebroadcast.

### What if unit_sats is below Bitcoin’s relay dust threshold? [UNRESOLVED]

- Why it matters: DUST-20 permits any positive unit_sats, but Bitcoin nodes will not relay outputs below the standard dust limit for their script type.
- Safe posture: A deploy with a very small unit_sats can be valid to an indexer yet unspendable in practice. Check the dust threshold for your output type before deploying.

## Indexer pipeline

### Observe — Ingest raw chain events [UNIVERSE]

Read complete blocks with input values, output values and output addresses, plus authoritative inscription identity. Record the transaction, output, inscription association and block position before declaring anything about balances.

### Normalize — Parse strictly and keep failures visible [UNIVERSE]

Apply the flat-string-object reader, exact key sets and canonical integer parsing. Keep parse failures as recorded invalid events rather than dropping them into an unexplained empty result.

### Resolve — Resolve deployment and history [UNIVERSE]

Fold the ticker to its identity, apply first-deploy-wins, and check the mint against the resolved unit size, the per-mint cap and remaining supply. Do not guess when two candidates conflict.

### Materialize — Create allocation records with position [UNIVERSE]

An allocation is an outpoint, a ticker, an amount, a unit size and a satoshi offset inside that output. The offset is not optional bookkeeping — it is what makes the next spend computable.

### Propagate — Follow satoshis through each spend [UNIVERSE]

Concatenate input values into one range and output values into another, intersect each allocation span with each output, keep only whole units, and record the difference as burned. Emit transfer effects only where the owning address actually changes.

### Reconcile — Roll forward and roll back [UNIVERSE]

Track block association so a reorg can invalidate newest first, reverse mutations, restore spent allocations, remove orphaned ones and replay the replacement branch. Preserve enough history to explain every transition.

## Safety requirements

- [critical] Never share a recovery phrase or private key: No DUST-20 application needs your seed phrase or private key. An app can prepare an unsigned transaction without them. Leave immediately if a site asks for either.
- [critical] Review every output role before signing: Before the wallet prompt appears you should be able to see the receiver, the units and satoshis going to them, your colored change, the ordinary bitcoin funding the fee, and the fee itself. A list of addresses is not a review.
- [critical] Missing colored change is a stop sign: If you are sending part of an allocation and no colored change output is present, the remainder is not kept — it is burned. This is not a formatting detail. Do not approve it.
- [high] Keep fee funding separate from colored inputs: Fund the miner fee from ordinary bitcoin. If the fee is taken out of colored backing, the colored range shifts and units can be destroyed even though the transaction confirms.
- [high] Revalidate outputs immediately before building: A selected output may have been spent since the screen loaded. A marketplace listing is discovery data, not proof that an output is still unspent. Re-check at build time, not at page load.
- [high] Treat source disagreement as a blocking error: If two indexers describe the same output differently, do not pick the friendlier answer. Show the conflict, block the irreversible step, and keep redacted evidence for investigation.
- [high] Do not downgrade an ambiguous construction to a warning: Unexplained satoshi differences, mixed-ticker selections and unattributable outputs are failures. Silently filling in a field, rounding a satoshi value, or assuming an unspecified payload is canonical converts a caught bug into a burned balance.
- [medium] Never blindly retry an uncertain broadcast: Keep the transaction id and known status. Disable repeat submission until someone has inspected the transaction. A duplicate broadcast can spend the same colored inputs a second way.
- [medium] Remember that confirmed is not permanent: A reorg can remove a confirmation and change which transaction actually spent an output. Track confirmation depth and invalidate derived state when the chain moves under you.

## Conformance summary

31 executable cases are published at https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/conformance.json and rendered at https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/dust-20/conformance.html.

- deploy-valid: ACCEPT — Valid deploy. Every field is a canonical integer string and max_sats equals supply × unit_sats.
- deploy-no-limit: ACCEPT — Valid deploy with lim_sats omitted. lim_sats is optional. Omitting it means there is no per-mint cap.
- deploy-zero-limit: ACCEPT — lim_sats of "0" means no cap. Zero is explicitly "no limit", not a cap of zero satoshis.
- deploy-arithmetic-mismatch: REJECT (max_sats_mismatch) — Arithmetic mismatch in max_sats. max_sats must equal supply × unit_sats exactly. Being one satoshi low usually means the builder used floating-point arithmetic.
- deploy-missing-max-sats: REJECT (missing_field) — Deploy missing max_sats. max_sats is required. Earlier documentation reported this as an unreconciled compatibility split; the current implementation rejects the payload rather than deriving the value.
- deploy-unknown-field: REJECT (unknown_field) — Deploy carrying an unknown field. Operations declare exact key sets. An unknown field is rejected, not ignored, so one payload cannot be read two ways.
- deploy-leading-zero: REJECT (bad_integer) — Malformed integer with a leading zero. Integers are canonical decimal strings. "0546" is not canonical even though it parses.
- deploy-float: REJECT (bad_integer) — Fractional unit_sats. Satoshis are indivisible. Decimal points are rejected outright.
- deploy-zero-supply: REJECT (bad_integer) — Zero supply. supply must be a positive integer. Zero and negative values are rejected.
- deploy-negative: REJECT (bad_integer) — Negative unit_sats. A minus sign is not part of a canonical DUST-20 integer.
- deploy-exceeds-money: REJECT (exceeds_money_supply) — Backing exceeds Bitcoin’s monetary supply. max_sats of 10,000,000,000,000,000 exceeds the 2,100,000,000,000,000 satoshis that will ever exist. The arithmetic is self-consistent but unbackable.
- deploy-limit-above-max: REJECT (lim_sats_above_max) — lim_sats greater than max_sats. A per-mint cap larger than the entire backing is contradictory.
- deploy-tick-whitespace: REJECT (bad_tick) — Ticker containing whitespace. Tickers exclude whitespace, control characters and the URL delimiters / ? # \ so an identity is always addressable.
- deploy-duplicate-ticker: REJECT (duplicate_deployment) — Redeploying an existing ticker. Identity is the NFC form folded to lower case, so "DUST" is the same ticker as "dust". The first valid deployment wins.
- mint-valid: ACCEPT — Valid mint with matching output. sats equals amt × unit_sats, and the observed output value equals sats.
- mint-case-insensitive-tick: ACCEPT — Mint naming the ticker in a different case. The mint resolves against the folded identity, so casing does not prevent resolution.
- mint-sats-mismatch: REJECT (mint_sats_mismatch) — Declared sats do not match the deployment ratio. 100 units at 546 satoshis is 54,600, not 54,000.
- mint-output-mismatch: REJECT (output_value_mismatch) — Output value differs from declared sats by one satoshi. The payload is internally consistent, but the real Bitcoin output holds 54,599 satoshis. The mint is invalid and cannot be repaired after broadcast.
- mint-limit-violation: REJECT (mint_exceeds_limit) — Mint exceeds lim_sats. 55,146 satoshis exceeds the declared per-mint cap of 54,600.
- mint-exceeds-supply: REJECT (mint_exceeds_supply) — Mint exceeds remaining supply. 999,950 units are already minted, so only 50 remain. The mint is rejected in full rather than partially filled.
- mint-no-deployment: REJECT (deployment_missing) — Mint for a ticker that was never deployed. A mint must resolve exactly one accepted deployment. Without it there is no unit size to check against.
- mint-missing-field: REJECT (missing_field) — Mint missing the sats field. sats is required. It is never inferred from amt, even though the ratio is known.
- mint-zero-amount: REJECT (bad_integer) — Mint of zero units. amt must be a positive integer.
- unknown-operation: REJECT (bad_operation) — Unknown operation. Only deploy and mint exist. Any other op is rejected.
- transfer-inscription: REJECT (bad_operation) — A transfer inscription. No transfer inscription is valid. Movement happens by spending the satoshis that carry the units. Earlier documentation listed a canonical transfer payload as an open question; the current implementation answers it by accepting none.
- wrong-protocol: REJECT (bad_protocol) — A different protocol identifier. Content whose p is not dust-20 is not a DUST-20 message.
- non-string-value: REJECT (not_flat_strings) — A numeric JSON value. Every value must be a JSON string. A bare number is rejected because JSON numbers cannot carry large integers exactly.
- duplicate-key: REJECT (duplicate_key) — A repeated field. A duplicate key is rejected rather than resolved last-wins, because two readers would otherwise disagree about the amount.
- trailing-content: REJECT (trailing_content) — Trailing content after the object. Content after the closing brace makes the message ambiguous and is rejected.
- nested-object: REJECT (not_flat_strings) — A nested object. A payload is a flat object of strings. Nesting is rejected.
- not-json: REJECT (not_object) — Content that is not a JSON object. Inscription content must parse as a single JSON object.
